paper.title: The observed-data likelihood of ADAM and iETS with unobserved periods: entropy term, SSOE Kalman filter and multiplicative approximations

definitions.definition: State space form of a time series model, also called the innovations form, in which the observation equation and the state transition share one error term $\epsilon_t$ per period: $z_t = w(\mathbf v_{t-\mathbf l}) + r(\mathbf v_{t-\mathbf l})\epsilon_t$, $\mathbf v_t = f(\mathbf v_{t-\mathbf l}) + g(\mathbf v_{t-\mathbf l})\epsilon_t$.

A period $t$ at which the potential value $z_t$ of the modelled variable is not observed ($O_t=0$): a period with zero demand in an intermittent demand model, where the demand size is not observed, or a period with a missing value.
The joint density of the observed data only, obtained by integrating the complete-data likelihood over the values at the unobserved periods.

The objective of the iETS estimator of Svetunkov and Boylan (2023, eq. B.6): the sum of the one-step log-densities of the observed demand sizes, minus the differential entropy $H_z(\hat\mu_t,\sigma)$ of the size at each period with zero demand, plus the Bernoulli log-likelihood of the occurrence.

The estimator used in ADAM and in iETS (Svetunkov and Boylan 2023, Appendix C): the single source of error recursion run with $\epsilon_t=0$ at the unobserved periods and with the fixed persistence vector $\mathbf g$ at the observed ones, with the likelihood taken as the product of one-step densities at the observed periods.

Pure multiplicative exponential smoothing in the form of the Augmented Dynamic Adaptive Model, in which each component $k$ is updated by the factor $(1+\epsilon_t)^{g_k}$, for instance $l_t = l_{t-1}b_{t-1}^{\phi}(1+\epsilon_t)^{\alpha}$.

Pure multiplicative exponential smoothing in the form of Hyndman et al. (2008), in which each component $k$ is updated by the factor $1+g_k\epsilon_t$, for instance $l_t = l_{t-1}b_{t-1}^{\phi}(1+\alpha\epsilon_t)$.

The recursion for the conditional mean $\mathbf a_t$ and scaled covariance $\mathbf P_t$ of the state of a linear single source of error model: at an observed period $v_t = z_t-\mathbf w'\mathbf a_t$, $f_t = \mathbf w'\mathbf P_t\mathbf w+1$, $\mathbf k_t=(\mathbf F\mathbf P_t\mathbf w+\mathbf g)/f_t$, $\mathbf a_{t+1}=\mathbf F\mathbf a_t+\mathbf k_t v_t$, $\mathbf P_{t+1}=\mathbf F\mathbf P_t\mathbf F'+\mathbf g\mathbf g'-\mathbf k_t\mathbf k_t'f_t$; at an unobserved period $\mathbf a_{t+1}=\mathbf F\mathbf a_t$, $\mathbf P_{t+1}=\mathbf F\mathbf P_t\mathbf F'+\mathbf g\mathbf g'$; started from $\mathbf a_1=\mathbf x_0$, $\mathbf P_1=\mathbf 0$.

The change $d_t=\log(\mu_t/\hat\mu_t)$ of the logarithm of the location of a pure multiplicative model accumulated over the unobserved periods since the last observed period, relative to the point forecast $\hat\mu_t$ with zero errors.

Approximate predictive density of a demand size after $j_t-1$ unobserved periods: the one-step density $f_z(z_t\mid\hat\mu_t e^{d})$ mixed over a normal [[D9:drift of the states]] $d\sim\mathcal N(m_t,w_t)$, with $m_t$, $w_t$ computed by 32-node Gauss-Legendre quadrature on the quantile function of $1+\epsilon$ and the mixture by Gauss-Hermite quadrature.

claims.statement: In the [[D1:single source of error form]] with every period observed, the state vector at time $t$ is a deterministic function of the initial states, the parameters and the observations up to $t$, so that the exact likelihood is the product of the one-step-ahead error densities.
The iETS estimator of Svetunkov and Boylan (2023) for intermittent demand maximises the [[D4:entropy-augmented likelihood]], motivated by analogy with the EM algorithm.
The fixed points of the EM algorithm are stationary points of the [[D3:observed-data likelihood]].
ADAM and iETS estimate models with [[D2:unobserved period]]s by the [[D5:zero-error recursion]].

For a model of intermittent demand $y_t=o_tz_t$ with Bernoulli occurrence $o_t\sim\text{Bernoulli}(p_t)$ independent of a continuous size $z_t$, the [[D3:observed-data likelihood]] is $\sum_{O_t=1}\log f(z_t\mid Y_{t-1};\theta) + \sum_{O_t=1}\log p_t + \sum_{O_t=0}\log(1-p_t)$, in which the unobserved sizes do not appear and the size and occurrence parts separate.

scope.population: models of intermittent demand $y_t=o_tz_t$ (iETS, ADAM with an occurrence part)
conditions: Bernoulli occurrence independent of a continuous demand size

claims.statement: The stationary points of the [[D4:entropy-augmented likelihood]] of iETS differ in general from those of the [[D3:observed-data likelihood]], because the entropy term $-H_z(\theta)$ has a non-zero gradient in the parameters while the cross-entropy of the EM E-step has zero gradient at the current estimate.

scope.population: iETS estimated by the entropy-augmented likelihood
conditions: sizes unobserved at the periods with zero demand

relations.locator: Appendix B, eq. B.6 (likelihood with the differential entropy of the unobserved sizes, derived by analogy with the EM algorithm)

claims.statement: For normally distributed demand sizes with fixed location, the maximiser in the variance of the [[D4:entropy-augmented likelihood]] is $\frac{T_1}{T}\hat\sigma^2$, where $\hat\sigma^2=\frac{1}{T_1}\sum_{O_t=1}e_t^2$ is the fixed point of the EM algorithm, $T$ the number of periods and $T_1$ the number of periods with observed sizes.

scope.population: iETS with normally distributed demand sizes
conditions: location of the sizes held fixed
variance as the only free parameter

claims.statement: With a dynamic model for the scale, the [[D4:entropy-augmented likelihood]] of iETS is unbounded, because the entropy terms of the periods with zero demand reward a scale going to zero for the normal distribution and to infinity for the Gamma distribution.

scope.population: iETS with a dynamic model for the scale of the demand sizes
conditions: normal or Gamma distribution of the sizes

claims.statement: With the differential entropy defined as $H=-\E\log f$, the sign of the entropy term in equations 29 and B.6 of Svetunkov and Boylan (2023) should be negative.

relations.locator: eq. 29 and eq. B.6 (sign of the entropy term)

scope.population: iETS objective of Svetunkov and Boylan (2023)

claims.statement: For a pure additive single source of error model with normal errors and [[D2:unobserved period]]s, the [[D8:SSOE Kalman filter]] gives $z_t\mid Y_{t-1}\sim\mathcal N(\mathbf w'\mathbf a_t,\sigma^2 f_t)$ at the observed periods, the exact observed-data log-likelihood $-\frac12\sum_{O_t=1}[\log(2\pi\sigma^2f_t)+v_t^2/(\sigma^2f_t)]$, and the concentrated variance $\hat\sigma^2=\frac{1}{T_1}\sum_{O_t=1}v_t^2/f_t$.

scope.population: pure additive single source of error models (ETS with additive components, ARIMA, regression)
scope.data_type: univariate time series with unobserved periods
conditions: initial states treated as fixed parameters
excludes: models mixing additive and multiplicative components

relations.locator: Kalman filter for state space models with correlated disturbances
Kalman filter for state space models with correlated disturbances

claims.statement: When every period is observed, the [[D8:SSOE Kalman filter]] keeps $\mathbf P_t=\mathbf 0$, has gain $\mathbf k_t=\mathbf g$ and $f_t=1$, and coincides with the single source of error recursion and the likelihood of the one-step errors.

scope.population: pure additive single source of error models

claims.statement: For pure additive single source of error models with normal errors, [[D2:unobserved period]]s and persistence vector $\mathbf g\neq\mathbf 0$, the maximiser of the [[D5:zero-error recursion]] likelihood is not the maximum likelihood estimator, because the zero-error recursion uses error variance $\sigma^2$ instead of $\sigma^2f_t\geq\sigma^2$ and gain $\mathbf g$ instead of $\mathbf k_t$ at the observed periods after an unobserved one.

scope.population: pure additive single source of error models
scope.data_type: univariate time series with unobserved periods

relations.locator: Appendix C (estimation with zero errors at the unobserved periods)

claims.statement: For ETS(A,N,N) with smoothing parameter $\alpha$ and zero state covariance before an interval of $j$ periods, the gain of the [[D8:SSOE Kalman filter]] at the end of the interval is $\alpha_j=((j-1)\alpha^2+\alpha)/((j-1)\alpha^2+1)$, which equals $\alpha$ for $j=1$ and tends to one as $j$ grows.

scope.population: ETS(A,N,N)
conditions: zero state covariance before an interval of $j$ periods

claims.statement: In the [[D6:ADAM multiplicative ETS]], the logarithms of the observation and of the components follow a linear single source of error model with innovation $u_t=\log(1+\epsilon_t)$ and the measurement, transition and persistence of the corresponding additive model, whereas in the [[D7:conventional multiplicative ETS]] the innovation of component $k$ is $\log(1+g_k\epsilon_t)$, which is not proportional to $u_t$.

scope.population: pure multiplicative ETS in the ADAM and conventional forms

claims.statement: For the [[D6:ADAM multiplicative ETS]] with the log-normal distribution and [[D2:unobserved period]]s, the [[D8:SSOE Kalman filter]] applied to $\log z_t$, with the known error mean $-s/2$ added to the propagation and the prediction, gives the exact observed-data likelihood, and the maximum likelihood scale $s$ is the positive root of $(\sum b_t^2/f_t)s^2+T_1s-\sum(v_t^0)^2/f_t=0$, where $v_t(s)=v_t^0+sb_t$ is the filter's prediction error.

scope.population: pure multiplicative ETS in the ADAM form
scope.data_type: positive univariate time series with unobserved periods

claims.statement: For the [[D6:ADAM multiplicative ETS]] with the log-normal distribution and all periods observed, the maximum likelihood estimate of the scale is $\hat s=2(\sqrt{1+m}-1)$ with $m=\frac{1}{T_1}\sum\log^2(1+\epsilon_t)$.

scope.population: pure multiplicative ETS in the ADAM form

claims.statement: The log-normal scale estimator $2(1-\sqrt{1-m})$ used in ADAM, with $m=\frac{1}{T_1}\sum\log^2(1+\epsilon_t)$, is not the maximum likelihood estimator: it overestimates the scale $s$ by about 35% at $s=0.5$ (0.677 against 0.5 when $m=s+s^2/4$) and is undefined for $m>1$.

scope.population: pure multiplicative ETS in the ADAM form

relations.locator: estimator of the scale of the log-normal distribution

claims.statement: For pure multiplicative models with the Gamma, log-normal or inverse Gaussian distribution, if $1+e_t=(1+\epsilon_t)D_t$ with $D_t=e^{d_t}$ independent of $\epsilon_t$, $\E(1+\epsilon_t)=1$ and $\Var(1+\epsilon_t)=s$, then $\E(e_t^2)=(1+s)\E(D_t^2)-2\E(D_t)+1$, and for the inverse Gaussian distribution $\E(e_t^2/(1+e_t))=\E(D_t)-2+(1+s)\E(D_t^{-1})$.

scope.population: pure multiplicative models with Gamma, log-normal or inverse Gaussian errors

claims.statement: For iETS(M,N,N) in the [[D7:conventional multiplicative ETS]] form, the [[D10:normal-drift mixture density]] of the demand size after an interval had a largest Kullback-Leibler divergence per observation from the exact density of 0.00115 for the Gamma, 0.00448 for the log-normal and 0.00400 for the inverse Gaussian distribution, against 2.359, 5.947 and 47.545 for the one-step density.

scope.population: iETS(M,N,N) with Gamma, log-normal and inverse Gaussian sizes
conditions: states known at the previous observed period

assessments.rationale: Deterministic archived computation with a refinement check; one model, one grid, and values that differ from those first reported in the source draft.

claims.statement: On errors simulated with the [[D9:drift of the states]] of iETS(M,N,N) and 1000 observed sizes, the fixed-point moment estimator of the Gamma and inverse Gaussian scale had a median relative bias of +0.02% with no failed fits when the drift order $\E(j-1)\alpha^2s$ was at most 0.02, and failed in 18%, 52% and 71% of fits for drift orders of 0.02 to 0.1, 0.1 to 0.3 and above 0.3.

scope.population: iETS(M,N,N) with Gamma and inverse Gaussian sizes
conditions: errors simulated with the drift, outside a fitted model

assessments.rationale: Archived Monte Carlo study with 2000 replications per cell; groups by drift order are coarse.

claims.statement: For a model with an occurrence part and occurrence probability $p_t$, a prediction interval of the demand with coverage $c$ that counts the zeros as covered is an interval of the demand sizes with coverage $(c-(1-p_t))/p_t$, centred on the size forecast $\hat\mu_t$ rather than on the demand forecast $p_t\hat\mu_t$.

scope.population: models with an occurrence part (iETS, ADAM)
conditions: prediction interval of the demand that counts zeros as covered
Bernoulli occurrence independent of a continuous demand size

claims.statement: The point forecast with zero errors of the [[D6:ADAM multiplicative ETS]] is not the conditional mean, because $\E(1+\epsilon_t)^{g_k}<1$ for $0<g_k<1$; for ETS(M,N,N) with Gamma errors of mean one and variance $s$ the conditional mean $h$ steps ahead is $\hat\mu_{T+h}[\Gamma(1/s+\alpha)s^{\alpha}/\Gamma(1/s)]^{h-1}$.

scope.population: pure multiplicative ETS in the ADAM form

claims.statement: For ETS(M,N,N) in the [[D6:ADAM multiplicative ETS]] form with Gamma errors, $s=0.32$ and $\alpha=0.21$, the approximate upper bound of the 90% prediction interval divided by the point forecast was 2.431 against 1.807 from simulated paths twelve steps ahead, and 2.616 against 1.638 after six unobserved periods at the end of the sample.

scope.population: ETS(M,N,N) in the ADAM form

assessments.rationale: Archived simulation with 1,000,000 paths; one parameter setting.

claims.statement: With a single source of error, the scaled state covariance $\mathbf P_t$ of the [[D8:SSOE Kalman filter]] has rank at most the number of [[D2:unobserved period]]s since it last vanished, which allows a low-rank factor $\mathbf P_t=\mathbf U_t\mathbf U_t'$ with a rank-one update at each observed period.

scope.population: linear single source of error models
scope.data_type: univariate time series with unobserved periods

claims.statement: For ADAM ETS(A,N,A) with lags 24 and 168 (193 state cells) on 1344 hourly observations generated by ETS(A,N,A), the low-rank factor form of the [[D8:SSOE Kalman filter]] was 10.55 times faster than the full covariance form for one missing value and 3.50 times faster for 48, with log-likelihoods equal to within 4.5e-13.

scope.population: ADAM ETS(A,N,A) with double seasonality
scope.data_type: hourly time series with missing values

assessments.rationale: Archived timing with 25 interleaved repetitions; one machine and one model configuration.

claims.statement: The smooth package for R and Python implements the [[D3:observed-data likelihood]] without the entropy term, the [[D8:SSOE Kalman filter]] for the pure additive models with the normal distribution and in logarithms for the [[D6:ADAM multiplicative ETS]] with the log-normal distribution, the [[D10:normal-drift mixture density]] with moment-equation scales for the other pure multiplicative models, and the corrected log-normal scale, in one C++ routine shared by both languages.

scope.setting: smooth package for R and Python, master branch at commit 8a5fbbb3

assessments.rationale: Implementation exists in the public repository; correctness relies on the package tests, not on independent verification.

claims.statement: In the smooth package, the [[D8:SSOE Kalman filter]] replaces the fitter only in the last forward pass after backcasting of the initial states, so that fits of series without [[D2:unobserved period]]s are unchanged.

scope.setting: smooth package for R and Python

assessments.rationale: Follows from the complete-data identity and the implementation design; equality to the last bit is stated, not documented by a test reported in the source.

claims.statement: For the pure additive models with the Laplace, S and Generalised Normal distributions, the smooth package keeps the error in its family with scale $sf_t^{1/p}$, and the Kullback-Leibler divergence of this approximation from the exact density is 0.0491 for the Laplace distribution and 0.260 for the S distribution at $f_t=4$.

scope.population: pure additive ADAM models with Laplace, S or Generalised Normal errors

assessments.rationale: Deterministic archived computation with an integration refinement check.

claims.statement: The errors $\epsilon_t$ of the single source of error model are independent across periods.
In the intermittent demand model the occurrence $o_t$ is independent of the potential demand size $z_t$.
The potential demand size $z_t$ has a continuous distribution, so that $P(z_t=0)=0$.
Whether a period is observed carries no information about the unobserved value $z_t$ beyond the model, so that the missing values are missing at random.
The initial states of the single source of error model are fixed parameters, so that the state covariance is zero at the start of the sample.
The errors of the pure additive model are normally distributed with constant variance $\sigma^2$.
In the log-normal ADAM multiplicative ETS, $\log(1+\epsilon_t)\sim\mathcal N(-s/2,s)$, so that $\E(1+\epsilon_t)=1$.
The [[D9:drift of the states]] of a pure multiplicative model over an interval is approximately normally distributed, with the states known at the previous observed period.

For iETS(M,N,N) in the [[D6:ADAM multiplicative ETS]] form, the [[D10:normal-drift mixture density]] of the demand size after an interval had a largest Kullback-Leibler divergence per observation from the exact density of 0.01452 for the Gamma and 0.00045 for the inverse Gaussian distribution, and is exact for the log-normal distribution, against 4.584, 18.635 and 630.772 for the one-step density.

scope.population: iETS(M,N,N) with Gamma, log-normal and inverse Gaussian sizes
conditions: states known at the previous observed period

assessments.rationale: Deterministic archived computation with a refinement check; one model and one grid.

claims.statement: Within iETS(M,N,N) models fitted by the [[D5:zero-error recursion]], updating the states with the persistence vector $\mathbf g$ after an interval raised the estimate of the Gamma and inverse Gaussian scale from the moment equation solved by bisection by more than three Monte Carlo standard errors in 97 of 120 cells, with a median increase in relative bias of 12.8 percentage points.

scope.population: iETS(M,N,N) with Gamma and inverse Gaussian sizes

assessments.rationale: Archived Monte Carlo study; 120 cells with 100 observed sizes.

claims.statement: For ETS(M,N,N) in the [[D7:conventional multiplicative ETS]] form with Gamma errors, $s=0.32$ and $\alpha=0.21$, the approximate upper bound of the 90% prediction interval divided by the point forecast was 2.431 against 2.393 from simulated paths twelve steps ahead, and 2.616 against 2.536 after six unobserved periods at the end of the sample.

scope.population: ETS(M,N,N) in the conventional form

assessments.rationale: Archived simulation with 1,000,000 paths; one parameter setting.

claims.statement: For ADAM ETS(A,N,A) with lags 24 and 168 on 1344 hourly observations following a fixed sine pattern, the low-rank factor form of the [[D8:SSOE Kalman filter]] was 2.96 times faster than the full covariance form for one missing value and 0.72 times as fast for 48, and slower than the full form above about 30 missing values.

scope.population: ADAM ETS(A,N,A) with double seasonality
scope.data_type: hourly time series with missing values
conditions: data following a fixed sine pattern

assessments.rationale: Archived timing with 25 interleaved repetitions; one machine and one model configuration.

claims.statement: At variance ratio $f_t=4$, the 16-node Gauss-Hermite mixture of the error density over normal state uncertainty had a Kullback-Leibler divergence from the exact density of 0.0081 for the Laplace and 0.113 for the S distribution, against 0.0491 and 0.260 for the error kept in its family with scale $sf_t^{1/p}$.

steps.statement: $P(y_t=0\mid Y_{t-1})=(1-p_t)\int f(z\mid Y_{t-1})dz=1-p_t$
$y_t>0$ has density $p_tf(y_t\mid Y_{t-1})$
The joint density of the observed data is the product of these conditional terms

evidence.description: Analytical derivation in the source draft (artefact A1).

steps.statement: $Q(\theta\mid\theta^{(k)})$ contains at each zero the cross-entropy $\int f_z^{(k)}\log f_z\,dz=-H_z(\theta^{(k)})-\KL(f_z^{(k)}\|f_z)$
$\partial_\theta\int f_z\log f_z^{\theta}dz|_{\theta=\theta^{(k)}}=\partial_\theta\int f_z\,dz=0$
$\nabla Q(\theta\mid\theta^{(k)})|_{\theta^{(k)}}=\nabla\ell(\theta^{(k)})$, so EM fixed points are stationary points of $\ell$
$-\partial_\theta H_z(\theta)\neq0$ in general (e.g. in the scale), adding to the score of $\ell$

evidence.description: Analytical derivation in the source draft (artefact A1).

steps.statement: $H_z=\frac12\log(2\pi e\sigma^2)$ for the normal distribution
$\partial\ell_H/\partial\sigma^2=-\frac{T_1}{2\sigma^2}+\frac{\sum e_t^2}{2\sigma^4}-\frac{T_0}{2\sigma^2}$, zero at $\sigma^2=\sum e_t^2/T$
EM iterates $\sigma^2_{(k+1)}=(\sum e_t^2+T_0\sigma^2_{(k)})/T$ with fixed point $\frac{1}{T_1}\sum e_t^2$

evidence.description: Analytical derivation in the source draft (artefact A1).

steps.statement: $(\mathbf x_{t-1},z_t,\mathbf x_t)$ is jointly Gaussian given $Y_{t-1}$
$\E(z_t\mid Y_{t-1})=\mathbf w'\mathbf a_t$, $\Var(z_t\mid Y_{t-1})=\sigma^2f_t$, $\Cov(\mathbf x_t,z_t\mid Y_{t-1})=\sigma^2(\mathbf F\mathbf P_t\mathbf w+\mathbf g)$
Conditioning on $z_t$ gives the update; unobserved periods only propagate
The likelihood follows from the observed-data decomposition, and $\sigma^2$ concentrates out because $f_t$, $\mathbf k_t$ do not depend on it

steps.statement: $\log z_t$ follows a linear Gaussian SSOE model with known error mean $-s/2$

The score in $s$ times $2s^2$ gives $(\sum b_t^2/f_t)s^2+T_1s-\sum(v_t^0)^2/f_t=0$

evidence.description: Monte Carlo study of the scale of Gamma and inverse Gaussian iETS(M,N,N) sizes under the ADAM and conventional forms. Part A: 480 cells of simulated relative errors with drift ($s\in\{0.05,0.2,0.5,1\}$, $\alpha\in\{0.1,0.3,0.6\}$, intervals fixed at 2, 5 or 10 or geometric with occurrence probability 0.5 or 0.2, 100 or 1000 observed sizes), 2000 replications per cell, fixed-point iteration with tolerance 1e-10 and at most 100 iterations; a fit fails when an iterate is not positive and finite, the iteration does not converge, or the value leaves the admissible range. Part B: 120 cells within fitted models with $s\in\{0.05,0.5\}$ and 100 observed sizes. Cells are grouped by the drift order $\E(j-1)\alpha^2s$. The run recorded smooth commit f9d062ee with the claimset scripts not yet committed; the scripts are archived at commit f1de3ea1.
seeds: numpy SeedSequence(20261015), one child stream per cell
evidence.outputs: fixed-point estimator, 1000 observed sizes, by drift order: <=0.02 median relative bias +0.02%, 0% failed; 0.02-0.1 -0.06%, 18%; 0.1-0.3 -0.42%, 52%; >0.3 -0.43%, 71%. Within fitted models the gain update raised the relative bias in 97 of 120 cells by a median of 12.8 percentage points

warrants.text: With a dynamic scale model, the scale at each period with zero demand is a free function of the parameters and enters the entropy-augmented likelihood only through the term $-H_z$; for the normal distribution $-H_z=-\frac12\log(2\pi e\sigma^2)$ increases without bound as $\sigma\to0$, and for the Gamma distribution the entropy decreases in the scale for large values, so the objective has no finite maximum.

The expected log-density of an unobserved size is $\int f_z\log f_z\,dz$, which equals $-H_z$ when the differential entropy is $H_z=-\E\log f_z$; the term added for each zero therefore enters the objective with a negative sign.

The SSOE Kalman filter coincides with the single source of error recursion whenever its covariance is zero; the covariance starts at zero after backcasting and becomes non-zero only at an unobserved period, so on series without unobserved periods the last forward pass performs the same operations as the recursion.

limitations.statement: Within a model fitted by the zero-error recursion, the fixed-point moment estimate of the Gamma and inverse Gaussian scale is biased upwards, because the states after an interval are updated with gain $\mathbf g$ and part of the drift leaks into the following errors.
The low-rank timing comparison uses one model configuration and one series length on one cloud VM (Intel Xeon 2.80 GHz, 4 vCPUs).
